findings.summary: The reminders signal {count,maxId,maxResponseDate} does not reliably detect a reassign: PUT /api/orders/reminders/:id/reassign nulls response_date and responded_by and changes neither count nor maxId, so unless the reassigned row held the global max(response_date) the key is unchanged and another user's passively-open reminders tab won't refetch until the next detectable change or manual refresh. Non-blocking because the actor sees it immediately via a direct fetchAllReminders(), and the response-notification path (checkNewResponses) is unaffected since responses always advance max(response_date). The plan comment 'maxResponseDate catches responses/reassigns' overstates the reassign case.
findings.recommendation: Add a max-last-write term to the reminders signal (e.g. max(id) is insufficient; a max(updated-at) or max(date) term) or explicitly document the reassign staleness bound.

findings.summary: The orders signal {count,maxId} cannot detect in-place edits that change neither row count nor max id. Bounded to ~10 min by the every-5th-tick safety-net full refetch, matching the existing TTL_ORDERS 10-min cache window; no regression versus current behavior. By design.
findings.recommendation: None required; behavior is intentional and documented in the impact doc.
